# Temple Scroll Column 34 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 34 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**34:1** The chambers on the western side of the outer court shall be for the Israelites who ascend to the temple to worship before Me.

**34:2** They shall bring their offerings, their sacrifices, their votive offerings, and their freewill offerings.

**34:3** They shall eat in these chambers — they, their sons and daughters, their male servants and female servants.

**34:4** No foreigner shall eat of the holy things, for it is not permitted to him.

**34:5** The priests shall eat of the most holy things within the inner court; the holy things they shall eat in their designated chambers in the outer court.

**34:6** Each man shall eat in his designated place; they shall not intermingle.

**34:7** The priests shall not carry any of the holy food from their chambers into the outer court.

**34:8** They shall not profane My holy food; for it is holy, and they shall treat it as such.

**34:9** Any Israelite who brings a sacrifice shall approach the gate nearest to him.

**34:10** The Levites shall receive it from his hand at the gate and convey it to the priests at the altar.

**34:11** Each man shall bring his offering to the gate assigned to his tribe.

**34:12** He shall not enter through the gate of another tribe, for each tribe has its own gate.

**34:13** The sons of Levi shall stand at the gates to receive the offerings from the Israelites.

**34:14** They shall convey them to the altar and to the chambers, each offering to its proper place.

**34:15** No man shall appear before Me empty-handed in the outer court at the appointed festivals.

**34:16** Each shall give according to his means — according to the blessing that the LORD his God has bestowed upon him.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 34 establishes the sacrificial logistics of the outer court. Tribal gate assignments enforce social order. The Levitical mediation between laity and priesthood echoes Numbers 18. The closing verse parallels Deuteronomy 16:17 almost verbatim.*
